title: ISyncManager.add registers a remote by unique name, creates its channel, and rolls back the record if init() throws
content:
`ISyncManager.add` is the single entry point for attaching a remote drive. It persists the remote record, creates its channel through the channel factory, and calls `channel.init()`:

```typescript
add(
  name: string,
  collectionId: DriveCollectionId,
  channelConfig: ChannelConfig,
  filter?: RemoteFilter,
  options?: RemoteOptions,
  id?: string,
): Promise<Remote>;
```

- `name` is the unique key across the manager. Reusing one throws ``Remote with name '${name}' already exists``.
- `collectionId` identifies the drive; build it with `DriveCollectionId.forDrive(driveId, branch?)` (branch defaults to `"main"`).
- `filter` defaults to `{ documentId: [], scope: [], branch: "" }` — empty arrays and an empty branch string all mean "no restriction".
- `options` defaults to `{ sinceTimestampUtcMs: "0" }`, i.e. sync from the start of history.
- `id` defaults to a generated UUID.

The important behavior is the failure path: **if `channel.init()` throws, `add` rolls the remote back out of both the in-memory map and storage, then rethrows the original error.** There is no half-registered remote to clean up. Calling `add` after `shutdown()` throws `"SyncManager is shutdown and cannot add remotes"`.

Connect's `addRemoteDrive(url, driveId?, options?)` helper shows the canonical call. It reads `window.ph.reactorClient` and the sync manager, fetches `{ id, graphqlEndpoint }` from the URL, dedupes against `sync.list()`, then:

```typescript
await sync.add(
  crypto.randomUUID(),                 // name
  DriveCollectionId.forDrive(driveId),
  { type: "gql", parameters: { url: driveInfo.graphqlEndpoint } },
  undefined,                           // filter -> no restriction
  options?.pollBehavior ? { pollBehavior: options.pollBehavior } : undefined,
);
```

Note that Connect passes a random UUID as the name — the name is an internal handle, not a label. To remove a drive, find every remote whose `meta.collectionId.equals(...)` and call `sync.remove(remote.meta.name)`. Config validation is eager: a `"gql"` config missing `url` throws at `add` time, as does any optional parameter with the wrong type.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/04-Synchronization.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
